title: Best habit app, supportive developers, love it!
body:
I reckon I’ve tried almost every habit tracking app on the App Store, and this is the one I’ve settled on.  I’ve been using it for a year now and still happy as.  

For one, I love the fact that I can use it not just as a habit tracker but also a place to keep notes of things I’ve done (for example, when I mark exercise as done, I can put details of the exercise), and then I can review those notes (filtered by activity, or category, or just see all of them) in a diary-like view. To me this is gold, and the best implementation I’ve seen of this feature. In fact, I requested some changes to make it easier to see and edit notes attached to a habit, and the developer implemented what I asked and more - he pretty much filled all the gaps I identified. How good is that!?  

The reporting views (by week/ month/ year) are a delight, and checking off tasks as done is quick and easy (including adding notes).  

Only improvement I’ve not yet seen is the ability to mark a task as done for the day if it’s an x number per week or month (like a max number per day count).. so I can see if I’ve done something today without clicking into it and looking at the calendar.. but that’s a small inconvenience that I’m quite happy to live with.

Get this app - you won’t be disappointed.

author: Snow Anemone

title: Sleek and minimalistic design, effective habit tracker, and only gets better with updates over time!
body:
Disclaimer: Detailed Review ⬇️

After trying out a handful of other habit tracker apps, I discovered HelloHabit through an Instagram ad, and it was seriously exactly what I was looking for. I’ve been a Premium user for almost 4 months now, and all of the app’s features have really helped organize and gradually improve my daily life. 

I’m a big fan of statistics, so receiving weekly, monthly, and annual updates on my habit progresses are extremely satisfying to see. I also love that you can see a plethora of different statistics in each individual habit whenever you want.

I’ve rarely needed to contact their Support Team (available in-app), but when I have, they are always super informative, helpful, and quick to reply. Additional features have slowly been added over the time I’ve been using the app, and I’m excited for them to add more supported syncing with other apps, more new features, and more quality of life updates!

Some nitpicks, if any:
- The HelloHabit Team has delayed promised features in the past, and then were late to release said features, without any update or notice. But I don’t know how many people are on their team, and they possibly just bit off more than they could chew. I don’t blame them at all and I’m sure they were working overtime to push out the update asap.
- I encountered a bug where a good chunk of my (to-do) Activity Entries were lost and they couldn’t be recovered, but the Support Team was quick to reply and note it down.
- Free users have a more limited feature set. I upgraded to Premium almost immediately.

The Premium price tag can seem expensive, but in my honest opinion, it was worth every cent (at least for me). After all, developers have expenses, so I believe the price justifies the Premium features, the simple yet elegant user interface and design, and the advanced statistics you can view.

Some users are so entitled, impatient, and whiny. I’ve really enjoyed the HelloHabit app so far, and I know it’s only going to get even better in the future!

title: Great App!
body: Very happy with this app and its presentation. Very well made and very easy to understand with valid pricing. If I was to give one criticism it would be for the presentation of ticked off weekly, monthly and yearly goals in the ‘Habit Reports’ page. If one completes the habit 100% then it would be more motivational for the user to see the whole week blocked off instead of seeing just the day of the completion if the goal. This of course needs further discussion as it might be considered mispresentation to bkock off the whole time period. For example, if you have a yearly habit that is supposed to be completed 4 times a year then it would be nice to see the whole year blocked out once the habit is completed - and then simply doing an outline on the days that they have ticked off the habits. Idk how this would work but either way I love this app. I just felt slightly deflated when completing a monthly goal and then checking the ‘Habit Report’ page only seeing one day out of the month being ticked despite it being quite a big habit that i put high effort in across the month.

title: Shows promise
body:
TLDR: It’s like finding a promising indie game on Steam or itchio. It doesn’t have a generic, cookie-cutter design too.

The onboarding and habit creation are straight to the point. The UX is what I expect from a small independent organization — the biggest positive is its direct-ness. The UI still needs refinement (not to be confused with buggy, it’s stable). Do not be discouraged by how it looks.

At its current price point, there’s not much to consider. It’s priced the same as (or lower than) most subscription-based habit trackers.

If this is result of the current direction of the product, then its development should be worth following.

title: Fantastic habit tracker!
body:
I absolutely love this app! ADHD life saver ❤️  The visual grid tracking, the granular control over building good versus bad habits, and the built-in journal make it an incredibly powerful tool. It has been a huge help for my daily routine.

To make it a flawless experience, I’d love to see some future updates to the iOS widgets:

Interactive Main Widget: It would be amazing to check off habits right from the home screen, maybe with a fun visual pulse and a toggleable chime!

Quick-Append Journal Widget: A "Today" widget to quickly add a timestamp and note would be a game-changer for quick time tracking and combatting time blindness.

Overall, it's a beautifully built app with a fantastic foundation. Can't wait to see what the developers do next!

title: Love it, almost perfect.
body:
Everything is so concise, neat, and easy to organize. This has been the best app to help me with my crazy ADHD. I am so thankful to the developers seriously.

I'm really hoping for the "Templates" update to the journal, that you will implement some kind of system that automatically creates a recurring note for an individual habit. I have a habit for "Lifting" at the gym. I like that there is an option to add a note with a checklist to it to tick which target areas I did that day. The only thing is I have to recreate the checklist each day. It's so close to being optimal, if templates could automatically recur each day for people with checklists inside of specific habits, and log which items on the checklist were completed while refreshing for the next day, I think this app would be perfect.

Also maybe the ability to hide the streak count for specific habits from the home menu, and capitalized words for the custom units just for neatness sake.

You guys did an amazing job ❤️💕

title: Good with a few flaws
body:
This app is generally really good and it’s helped me a lot since getting it. But there’s one pretty significant feature missing, and it’s an option to pause habits and not lose your streak. For example if you become sick or go on a vacation and you can’t follow your regular habits and routine. It makes me feel guilty for losing my streaks, but like sometimes your routine has routine has to change for a few days! I feel like this would be fairly easy to implement and would make the app almost perfect to me. 

A way to set goals to be for a set amount of time (like exercising for 30 min for example) but still be able to check it off just once and not have to check off all the minutes would also be great. If my goal is to exercise for 30 min, I’m gonna do it all at once. I don’t want to have the click the check mark a bunch of times to get to it completed. 

If those two features were added it would be a perfect 5 stars to me!

title: A ton of potential!
body:
This app has a lot of potential and I will keep using it but it has to major flaws when it comes to habit tracking.

1 - you can’t track using decimals. So if you walk 0.5 miles you’re forced to either not track it or round up. Both bad options. Same would go for tracking drinks, water intake etc.

2 - you can’t archive habits. So if you have a short term goal you’re working on, once it’s completed you either have to delete it or just have it cluttering the screen. Another major con for me.

Otherwise it has a lot of good features and is worth the $20 for the year but I will continue searching for something that has a little more flexibility in tracking individual habits.

author: Sadiects

title: Loving it so far!
body: I’ve been using the app for a while now and I’m really liking it. I’ve been using it more for breaking habits than building and it’s been really helpful to be able to make notes about the circumstances when I slip up. It could use a few improvements (the biggest one I would like is some more freedom on color choice. Letting us enter our own hex code would be awesome, but even just a bit more of the spectrum to choose from would be nice), but the dev is very nice and communicative so I’m sure there will be some good updates in the future. 🙂 (Also, I’m still really excited that it has my favorite font  - Montserrat. 😉)
author: Biyxtren

title: Smooth and Snappy
body: After using this app for about 2 weeks, I’ve found it’s very intuitive and easy to use. It keeps me on track with its notifications and the apple Health integration has made my gym habit tracking basically automatic which is great. The UI is nice and easy to use and feel really snappy to navigate through. The premium pricing is great as well, even though I have lifetime access, I believe this is well worth the money. The only thing its missing for me is home screen widgets, which the developer has assured me are coming in a future update so I’m very much looking forward forward to that!

title: Just got it, but love it so far!
body:
I’m really impressed with the thoroughness and attention to details on the features and types of habits.

Loves:
- I love the automatic tracking of steps, calories, etc. via health and Apple Watch especially! I loaded that up and it picked up historical data. I love being able to see the stats! 
- Letting the user choose day of the week to start week on
- incorporating of activity and adhoc notes into the journal

Will update over time :)
